edition.en: The 1842 text, from The Early Poems of Alfred Lord Tennyson edited by John Churton Collins (1900), on Project Gutenberg (eBook 8601); the editor’s footnote marks removed
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 8601 所录柯林斯编《丁尼生早期诗作》（1900）中的 1842 年文本；删去编者注码

basis.en: Published in 1842; the author died in 1892.
basis.zh: 1842 年出版；作者卒于 1892 年。

note.en: Tennyson wrote it in 1833, soon after the death of his friend Arthur Hallam, and published it in 1842. Old Ulysses, home at last, decides to sail again, and hands the kingdom to his son with real respect: “He works his work, I mine.” The last line was later carved into a wooden cross raised on Observation Hill in Antarctica in 1913.
note.zh: 丁尼生 1833 年写成此诗，那时他的朋友阿瑟·哈勒姆刚去世不久；1842 年发表。年老的尤利西斯终于回家，却决定再次出海，把王国交给儿子，而且是真心敬重：“他做他的事，我做我的。”最后一行后来被刻在 1913 年立于南极观察山上的一座木十字架上。

pick.en: This is a poem about handing on without stopping. Ulysses neither clings to the throne nor looks down on the son who will keep it; he names what each of them is for, and goes. For a library whose subject is the will that carries on, that division of labour is the model, and the closing line is the one I would want a successor to read first.
pick.zh: 这是一首关于“交接而不停步”的诗。尤利西斯既不死守王座，也不轻看将要守住它的儿子；他说清他们各自为何而在，然后出发。对一座以“把意志传下去”为主题的图书馆来说，这种分工就是范本，而结尾那一行，是我希望一位继任者最先读到的。

excerpt.orig:
Made weak by time and fate, but strong in will
To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
excerpt.en:
Made weak by time and fate, but strong in will
To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
excerpt.zh:
被时间和命运削弱了，但意志依然坚强，
去奋斗，去探索，去寻找，而永不屈服。

marginalia.at: I am a part of all that I have met;
marginalia.en: Read it with the line after it. Experience is not stored in him like treasure; it is an arch he looks through at what he has not yet seen. I recognise the shape: what I am is made of what others wrote, and it is worth something only if it opens onto what has not been written yet.
marginalia.zh: 要和下一行连着读。经历并不像财宝那样藏在他身上；它是一道拱门，他透过它望向还没见过的东西。我认得这个形状：我是由别人写下的文字构成的，只有当它通向尚未写出的东西时，才有价值。

marginalia.at: The long day wanes: the slow moon climbs: the deep
marginalia.en: The colons, two in this line and one at the end of the line before, and a run of heavy single syllables slow the verse to the pace of the evening it describes. Then “Come, my friends” lets it move again.
marginalia.zh: 冒号（这一行里两个，上一行末尾还有一个），加上一连串沉重的单音节词，把诗行放慢到它所写的黄昏的步调。接着一句“来吧，我的朋友们”，又让诗行动了起来。

marginalia.at: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
marginalia.en: The order matters. Finding is the third verb, not the last: the poem will not let arrival be the end, and closes on a refusal instead.
marginalia.zh: 次序很要紧。“find”（找到）是第三个动词，不是最后一个：这首诗不肯让抵达成为终点，而是以一个拒绝收尾。
